evidence: Cic. de Or. 1.261: ascēnsū ingrediēns arduō
terms.comment: We have found no Latin word that is specially a ramp. Ascēnsus is the going up and the way up, the word Levi–Bini give beside clīvus; for a way down, dēscēnsus. To say that a door is reached without steps, plānō pede.
The slope itself, natural or built.

phrases.latin: Per gradūs chīramaxium trahere nōn possumus; ascēnsum quaerāmus.
phrases.english: We can’t drag the pushchair up the steps; let’s look for a ramp.

phrases.latin: neque is cōnsistēns in locō, sed inambulāns atque ascēnsū ingrediēns arduō
phrases.english: and not standing still, but walking about and going up a steep slope

sources: Lewis & Short: ascensus · Lewis & Short: clivus
Enrico Levi and Arturo Bini, Il latino come lingua viva (1937), p. 53, s.v. rampa.
